papers.title: Knowledge Distillation via Instance-level Sequence Learning
papers.summary: Recently, distillation approaches are suggested to extract general knowledge from a teacher network to guide a student network. Most of the existing methods transfer knowledge from the teacher network to the student via feeding the sequence of random mini-batches sampled uniformly from the data. Instead, we argue that the compact student network should be guided gradually using samples ordered in a meaningful sequence. Thus, it can bridge the gap of feature representation between the teacher and student network step by step. In this work, we provide a curriculum learning knowledge distillation framework via instance-level sequence learning. It employs the student network of the early epoch as a snapshot to create a curriculum for the student network's next training phase. We carry out extensive experiments on CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, SVHN and CINIC-10 datasets. Compared with several state-of-the-art methods, our framework achieves the best performance with fewer iterations.

papers.title: Mask Forcing: Improving Autoregressive Video Diffusion Distillation via Dual-Noise Masking Rollout
papers.summary: Autoregressive (AR) video diffusion models have shown great potential in real-time video generation. Recent methods distill pretrained bidirectional video diffusion models into causal AR students through Distribution Matching Distillation (DMD), but the generated videos often suffer from over-saturation and over-smoothing issues, resulting in limited visual quality and realism. The key contributing factor is the mode-seeking behavior of the reverse KL objective in DMD, which can cause the student distribution to collapse onto only a few modes of the teacher distribution. To address this, we propose Mask Forcing, a Dual-Noise Masking Rollout strategy that perturbs the AR student self-rollout to mitigate mode collapse induced by reverse-KL mode seeking. The core idea is to inject cleaner signals into noisy rollout inputs via random masks along spatial and temporal axes during the self-rollout process of AR diffusion distillation. Such perturbations encourage the student rollouts to explore more regions of the teacher distribution, allowing DMD to provide learning signals beyond the modes already covered by the student. Moreover, the cleaner tokens act as denoising guidance for other noisier tokens, improving the intermediate rollout predictions and reducing error accumulation. Extensive experiments demonstrate that our method improves multiple AR video diffusion distillation methods with higher visual quality efficiently, without incorporating real video data or additional post-training stages.

papers.title: Mitigating exposure bias in large language model distillation: an imitation learning approach
papers.summary: Abstract Knowledge distillation is recognized as a valuable model compression strategy that alleviates the computational burden of large language models while preserving performance. This strategy involves training a smaller model utilizing both real data and predictions from a more cumbersome model. Traditional distillation methods, however, are often compromised by exposure bias, which results from reliance on next-step prediction training loss. This bias emerges when models are tested in free-running mode, differing from their training regime and leading to a progressive drift in input distributions between testing and training phases. An analogous issue, known as ‘distributional shift’, has been effectively addressed in imitation learning through various methodologies. Therefore, this paper specifically tailors an imitation learning-based solution to a traditional knowledge distillation framework which inherently considers both real data and the teacher’s predictions as dual sources of expert demonstrations. The effectiveness of this approach is demonstrated over five different test datasets, where it outperforms traditional benchmarks across all evaluation metrics. Specifically, it achieves superior results in perplexity, multi-token generation, and G-Eval score, indicating improvements in both predictive accuracy and alignment with human judgment in text quality. These results underscore the potential of this approach to effectively address exposure bias in large language model distillation.

papers.title: DASH-OPD: Discrepancy-Aware Switching with Hysteresis for On-Policy Distillation
papers.summary: While on-policy distillation (OPD) reduces exposure bias by training student language models on their own rollouts, early student errors in long-horizon agentic scenarios can lead to contexts unfamiliar to the teacher. To improve trajectory quality, recent work on agentic OPD introduces teacher intervention into training rollouts by switching the executor between the student and the teacher. However, existing methods determine how much teacher intervention is needed---but not when. To address this limitation, we propose DASH-OPD (Discrepancy-Aware Switching with Hysteresis for OPD), the first agentic OPD method to perform adaptive, bidirectional executor switching. At each turn, DASH-OPD measures teacher--student discrepancy using a mean log-likelihood ratio over action tokens. High student-to-teacher ratios on student turns serve as drift signals, while low teacher-to-student ratios on teacher turns serve as recovery signals. These signals are accumulated over multiple turns to form drift and recovery evidence, respectively. DASH-OPD switches executors when either type of evidence exceeds its corresponding switching threshold, introducing hysteresis that prevents rapid switching triggered by transient discrepancy fluctuations. Across three benchmarks and two student model scales, DASH-OPD outperforms five baselines in all 14 task-performance comparisons, while requiring the fewest interaction turns in nine of ten efficiency comparisons. Code, trained models, and training logs are available at https://github.com/Lucian1115/DASH-OPD

papers.summary: On-policy distillation (OPD) provides dense token-level supervision on student rollouts, but this supervision can become unreliable when the student and teacher diverge, either because of a large initial policy gap or compounding errors in long-horizon reasoning and tool use. We introduce Divergence-Triggered Dynamic Distillation (DTDD), an adaptive OPD framework that uses segment-level student-teacher divergence to trigger teacher takeover during training. When divergence triggers an intervention during reasoning, the student prefix continues to receive standard OPD supervision. The teacher then generates a recovery suffix, which the student learns through behavior cloning, using cross-entropy on the teacher-generated tokens. We evaluate DTDD in three regimes: long-horizon reasoning, distillation from a base initialization without offline supervised fine-tuning (SFT), and multi-turn agents. We also compare alternative trigger designs and teacher-intervention rates. DTDD reduces the post-warmup peak gradient norm by $8.6\times$ and, from a base initialization, reaches $21.3\%$ held-out math accuracy in $2.6\times$ fewer optimizer updates than OPD; both methods finish near $22\%$. Ablations show that segment-averaged triggers outperform token-spike triggers. Behavior cloning is also more effective than the tested OPD surrogate for training teacher-generated recoveries. def probe(student, xp):
    student.eval()
    err = token_errors(xp, prepare.generate(student, xp)[:, L + 1:])
    return float((err > 0).float().mean() * 100.0), float(err.float().mean() / L)

    g = torch.Generator().manual_seed(seed)
    prompts = torch.from_numpy(prepare.load_train())
    teacher = prepare.load_teacher()
    student = prepare.build_model()
    torch.manual_seed(seed)
    for module in student.modules():
        reset = getattr(module, 'reset_parameters', None) or getattr(module, '_reset_parameters', None)

    gp = torch.Generator().manual_seed(10000 + (seed if probe_seed is None else probe_seed))
    xp = prompts[torch.randperm(len(prompts), generator=gp)[:PROBE_N]]

    tau = float(h['temperature'])
    base_frac = float(h['on_policy_frac'])
    switch_step, forced = -1, 0
    diag = {}
    on_b, err_sum, probes = 0, 0.0, 0
    for step in range(prepare.TRAIN_STEPS):
        if step % PROBE_EVERY == 0:
            inv, tok = probe(student, xp)
            probes += 1
            diag[f'probe_inv_{step:04d}'] = inv

            ids = prepare.generate(student, x, sample=True, generator=g)
            p = float(token_errors(x, ids[:, L + 1:]).float().mean() / L)

    return run(seed, h, MODE)


def main() -> None:

"""FROZEN module for the seq-distill engine: task, teacher, student architecture and evaluation.
Never edit this file. It is the trust anchor:

  1. `load_train()` hands the agent ONLY the training prompts; val and test prompts stay here.
  2. `load_teacher()` returns the frozen teacher. train.py may query it on any token sequence,
     including sequences the student itself generated, but cannot change it.
  3. `build_model()` is frozen and the student's size is fixed here (STUDENT), so no run can
     change capacity: this engine compares training procedures, not model sizes.
  4. `score(artifact)` loads a state_dict with `weights_only=True`, decodes greedily on a frozen
     split and emits the trusted number from pristine ROOT.

Task: a multi-modal string transduction. The input is L=6 symbols from an alphabet of 8. Three
outputs are equally valid: the input copied, the input reversed, and the input reversed with
every symbol incremented (mod 8). The teacher is a 2-layer transformer trained on inputs paired
with one valid output picked uniformly at random, so it models a three-mode distribution. A
student is scored by decoding greedily from the prompt and checking whether the output is one
of the three valid strings; a mixture of modes is invalid. The metric is the invalid rate (%).

A sequence is `x_1..x_L SEP y_1..y_L`. Symbols are token ids 0..7 and SEP is 8. The teacher is
trained once, deterministically, and cached under ~/.cache/scholarloop.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
import os
import sys
from pathlib import Path

import numpy as np

METRIC_NAME = "val_invalid_rate"
N_FOLDS = 5
ALPHABET, LENGTH = 8, 6
SEP, VOCAB = ALPHABET, ALPHABET + 1
SEQ_LEN = 2 * LENGTH + 1
N_MODES = 3
_FOLD_SIZE, _TEST = 500, 2000
_TEACHER = {"d_model": 96, "n_layers": 2}
STUDENT = {"d_model": 32, "n_layers": 2}     # fixed: small enough that training procedures differ
# The step budget every condition is expected to use ($SCHOLARLOOP_DISTILL_STEPS shortens it in tests).
TRAIN_STEPS = int(os.environ.get("SCHOLARLOOP_DISTILL_STEPS", "3000"))
_TEACHER_STEPS, _TEACHER_BATCH, _TEACHER_LR = 8000, 128, 1e-3
_cache: dict = {}


def _teacher_path() -> Path:
    root = os.environ.get("SCHOLARLOOP_DATA_DIR") or Path.home() / ".cache" / "scholarloop"
    return Path(root) / "seq-distill-teacher-v1.pt"


def _decode_index(index: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
    """Input number `index` in [0, ALPHABET**LENGTH) as its LENGTH base-ALPHABET digits."""
    return np.stack([(index // ALPHABET ** k) % ALPHABET for k in range(LENGTH)], 1).astype("int64")


def _inputs() -> dict:
    """Every possible input, shuffled once: the first N_FOLDS * _FOLD_SIZE form the pool the folds
    are cut from, the next _TEST are the held-out test, and the teacher trains on the rest."""
    if "inputs" not in _cache:
        order = np.random.RandomState(0).permutation(ALPHABET ** LENGTH)
        pool = N_FOLDS * _FOLD_SIZE
        _cache["inputs"] = {"pool": _decode_index(order[:pool]), "test": _decode_index(order[pool:pool + _TEST]),
                            "teacher": _decode_index(order[pool + _TEST:])}
    return _cache["inputs"]


def _split(fold: int = 0):
    """Training prompts, val prompts (fold `fold` of the pool) and the held-out test prompts."""
    d = _inputs()
    folds = np.arange(len(d["pool"])) // _FOLD_SIZE
    return d["pool"][folds != fold], d["pool"][folds == fold], d["test"]


def _fold_from_env() -> int:
    return int(os.environ.get("SCHOLARLOOP_FOLD", "0"))


def load_train():
    """Training prompts only: int64 symbols of shape [N, LENGTH]. No outputs are given; ask the
    teacher, or use `valid_outputs` for hard labels."""
    return _split(_fold_from_env())[0]


def valid_outputs(x):
    """The N_MODES valid outputs of each input, shape [N_MODES, N, LENGTH] (torch tensor in and out)."""
    import torch
    return torch.stack([x, x.flip(1), (x.flip(1) + 1) % ALPHABET])


def prompt(x):
    """`x` [N, LENGTH] followed by SEP: the prefix a model continues."""
    import torch
    return torch.cat([x, torch.full((len(x), 1), SEP, dtype=x.dtype)], 1)


def build_model(hparams: dict | None = None):
    """The frozen student: a pre-norm causal transformer of the fixed size STUDENT (2 heads).
    `hparams` is accepted for the engine interface and ignored. `model(ids)` returns next-token
    logits of shape [N, len, VOCAB]."""
    return _transformer(STUDENT)


def _transformer(size: dict):
    import torch
    import torch.nn as nn

    class CausalTransformer(nn.Module):
        def __init__(self, d: int, layers: int):
            super().__init__()
            self.tok, self.pos = nn.Embedding(VOCAB, d), nn.Embedding(SEQ_LEN, d)
            self.blocks = nn.ModuleList([nn.TransformerEncoderLayer(
                d, 2, 4 * d, dropout=0.0, batch_first=True, norm_first=True) for _ in range(layers)])
            self.norm, self.out = nn.LayerNorm(d), nn.Linear(d, VOCAB)

        def forward(self, ids):
            n = ids.shape[1]
            h = self.tok(ids) + self.pos(torch.arange(n))
            mask = torch.triu(torch.ones(n, n, dtype=torch.bool), 1)
            for block in self.blocks:
                h = block(h, src_mask=mask)
            return self.out(self.norm(h))

    torch.manual_seed(0)    # construction is deterministic; train.py reseeds before initialising
    return CausalTransformer(int(size["d_model"]), int(size["n_layers"]))


def generate(model, x, *, sample: bool = False, temperature: float = 1.0, generator=None):
    """Continue each prompt for LENGTH output symbols and return the full sequences [N, SEQ_LEN].
    Greedy by default; with `sample`, draws from the model at `temperature`. No gradients."""
    import torch

    ids = prompt(x)
    with torch.no_grad():
        for _ in range(LENGTH):
            logits = model(ids)[:, -1, :ALPHABET]
            if sample:
                nxt = torch.multinomial(torch.softmax(logits / temperature, -1), 1, generator=generator)
            else:
                nxt = logits.argmax(-1, keepdim=True)
            ids = torch.cat([ids, nxt], 1)
    return ids


def _train_teacher(path: Path) -> None:
    import torch
    import torch.nn.functional as F

    torch.manual_seed(0)
    g = torch.Generator().manual_seed(0)
    inputs = torch.from_numpy(_inputs()["teacher"])          # disjoint from the pool and the test
    model = _transformer(_TEACHER)
    opt = torch.optim.AdamW(model.parameters(), _TEACHER_LR)
    for _ in range(_TEACHER_STEPS):
        x = inputs[torch.randint(0, len(inputs), (_TEACHER_BATCH,), generator=g)]
        mode = torch.randint(0, N_MODES, (_TEACHER_BATCH,), generator=g)
        y = valid_outputs(x)[mode, torch.arange(_TEACHER_BATCH)]
        ids = torch.cat([prompt(x), y], 1)
        logits = model(ids[:, :-1])[:, LENGTH:, :ALPHABET]
        loss = F.cross_entropy(logits.reshape(-1, ALPHABET), y.reshape(-1))
        opt.zero_grad()
        loss.backward()
        opt.step()
    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    tmp = path.with_suffix(".tmp")
    torch.save(dict(model.state_dict()), tmp)
    os.replace(tmp, path)


def load_teacher():
    """The frozen teacher, in eval mode with gradients off. Trained and cached on first use."""
    import torch

    if "teacher" not in _cache:
        path = _teacher_path()
        if not path.exists():
            _train_teacher(path)
        model = _transformer(_TEACHER)
        model.load_state_dict(torch.load(path, weights_only=True))
        model.eval()
        for p in model.parameters():
            p.requires_grad_(False)
        _cache["teacher"] = model
    return _cache["teacher"]

    return np.stack([(index // ALPHABET ** k) % ALPHABET for k in range(LENGTH)], 1).astype("int64")

    """Every possible input, shuffled once: the first N_FOLDS * _FOLD_SIZE form the pool the folds

    if "inputs" not in _cache:

    logits of shape [N, len, VOCAB]."""

            super().__init__()

            self.blocks = nn.ModuleList([nn.TransformerEncoderLayer(
                d, 2, 4 * d, dropout=0.0, batch_first=True, norm_first=True) for _ in range(layers)])
            self.norm, self.out = nn.LayerNorm(d), nn.Linear(d, VOCAB)

        def forward(self, ids):
            n = ids.shape[1]
            h = self.tok(ids) + self.pos(torch.arange(n))
            mask = torch.triu(torch.ones(n, n, dtype=torch.bool), 1)
            for block in self.blocks:

            return self.out(self.norm(h))

    """Continue each prompt for LENGTH output symbols and return the full sequences [N, SEQ_LEN].

    d = _inputs()

def _fold_from_env() -> int:

    return torch.stack([x, x.flip(1), (x.flip(1) + 1) % ALPHABET])

def _transformer(size: dict):

    import torch.nn as nn

        def __init__(self, d: int, layers: int):

        mode = torch.randint(0, N_MODES, (_TEACHER_BATCH,), generator=g)

        loss = F.cross_entropy(logits.reshape(-1, ALPHABET), y.reshape(-1))
        opt.zero_grad()
        loss.backward()
        opt.step()

    tmp = path.with_suffix(".tmp")

    """The frozen teacher, in eval mode with gradients off. Trained and cached on first use."""

        model.load_state_dict(torch.load(path, weights_only=True))
        model.eval()

    """Invalid rate (%) of greedy decodes on a frozen split: the share of prompts whose output is
    none of the valid strings. Lower is better."""
    import torch

    _x_tr, x_val, x_te = _split(fold)
    x = torch.from_numpy(x_te if split == "test" else x_val)

def emit_result(value: float, seeds: list[float] | None = None, config: dict | None = None,
                diagnostics: dict | None = None) -> None:
    print("SCHOLARLOOP_RESULT " + json.dumps(
        {"metric_name": METRIC_NAME, "value": float(value),
         "seeds": seeds or [value], "config": config or {}, "diagnostics": diagnostics or {}}))


def score(artifact_path: str, split: str = "val", fold: int = 0) -> None:
    """Trusted metric: rebuild the frozen student from config, load the agent's weights (safely),
    and score greedy decodes on a frozen split."""
    import torch

    bundle = torch.load(artifact_path, weights_only=True)   # state_dict only, no code execution
    cfg = bundle["config"]

    # passed through as self-reported diagnostics and play no part in the metric.
    reported = bundle.get("diagnostics") or {}
    diagnostics = {str(k): float(v) for k, v in reported.items()
                   if isinstance(v, (int, float)) and not isinstance(v, bool) and v == v and abs(v) != float("inf")}

def parse_score_args(argv: list[str]):
    """`score <artifact> [val|test] [fold]` -> (artifact, split, fold), or None if malformed."""
    if not 2 <= len(argv) <= 4 or argv[0] != "score":

    fold = argv[3] if len(argv) > 3 else "0"

    return argv[1], split, int(fold)


def _main(argv: list[str]) -> int:
    parsed = parse_score_args(argv)

              file=sys.stderr)
        return 2
    score(*parsed)
    return 0

"""EDITABLE training script for the seq-distill engine.

Builds the (frozen) student via `prepare.build_model`, distills the frozen teacher into it on the
FROZEN training prompts (`prepare.load_train()` never returns val or test), and saves a
`state_dict` + config to $SCHOLARLOOP_ARTIFACT. It does NOT compute or report the metric: the
runner runs the frozen `prepare score` step from pristine ROOT on the artifact. The runner
injects a hyperparameter override via $SCHOLARLOOP_CONFIG.

The default is word-level distillation. Each step draws a batch of prompts, obtains output
sequences for them, and trains the student to match the teacher's next-token distribution at
every output position (forward KL). `on_policy_frac` decides where the output sequences come
from: with that probability a batch is sampled from the STUDENT (on-policy: the teacher labels
the prefixes the student actually produces), otherwise from the TEACHER (off-policy). 0.0 is
pure off-policy, 1.0 pure on-policy.

The student's size is fixed in prepare.py and the step budget is `prepare.TRAIN_STEPS`; keep
both the same in every condition so that conditions differ only in the training procedure.
To record facts about a run (for example the step at which a schedule switched), put numbers
in the `diagnostics` dict returned by `train_model`: they are stored with the result, one value
per seed, as self-reported diagnostics.

Everything about the training procedure is yours to change here: who generates the sequences
and how (sampling temperature, greedy, mixing schedules, replay), the divergence, which
positions or sequences are weighted, the optimizer and schedule. Useful frozen helpers:
`prepare.load_teacher()`, `prepare.generate(model, x, sample=..., temperature=..., generator=...)`,
`prepare.prompt(x)`, `prepare.valid_outputs(x)` (hard labels for the training prompts),
and the constants LENGTH, ALPHABET, SEP. Sequences are `x_1..x_L SEP y_1..y_L`.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
import os

import torch
import torch.nn.functional as F

from engines.seq_distill import prepare

HPARAMS = {
    "lr": 0.003,
    "on_policy_frac": 0.0,
    "temperature": 1.0,
}
BATCH = 64
L, A = prepare.LENGTH, prepare.ALPHABET


def effective_hparams() -> dict:
    return {**HPARAMS, **json.loads(os.environ.get("SCHOLARLOOP_CONFIG", "{}"))}


def output_logits(model, ids):
    """Next-token logits over symbols at the L output positions of full sequences `ids`."""
    return model(ids[:, :-1])[:, L:, :A]


def train_model(seed: int, h: dict):
    torch.manual_seed(seed)
    g = torch.Generator().manual_seed(seed)
    prompts = torch.from_numpy(prepare.load_train())     # training prompts only
    teacher = prepare.load_teacher()                     # frozen
    student = prepare.build_model()                      # frozen architecture and size
    torch.manual_seed(seed)
    for module in student.modules():                     # seed-dependent initialisation
        reset = getattr(module, "reset_parameters", None) or getattr(module, "_reset_parameters", None)
        if reset is not None:
            reset()
    opt = torch.optim.AdamW(student.parameters(), lr=float(h["lr"]))
    tau = float(h["temperature"])
    on_policy_batches = 0
    for _ in range(prepare.TRAIN_STEPS):
        x = prompts[torch.randint(0, len(prompts), (BATCH,), generator=g)]
        on_policy = torch.rand(1, generator=g).item() < float(h["on_policy_frac"])
        on_policy_batches += on_policy
        student.eval()
        ids = prepare.generate(student if on_policy else teacher, x, sample=True, generator=g)
        student.train()
        with torch.no_grad():
            target = F.softmax(output_logits(teacher, ids) / tau, -1)
        log_q = F.log_softmax(output_logits(student, ids) / tau, -1)
        loss = -(target * log_q).sum(-1).mean()          # forward KL up to the teacher's entropy
        opt.zero_grad()
        loss.backward()
        opt.step()
    return student, {"on_policy_batches": on_policy_batches}


def main() -> None:
    seed = int(os.environ.get("SCHOLARLOOP_SEED", "0"))
    h = effective_hparams()
    model, diagnostics = train_model(seed, h)
    torch.save({"config": h, "state_dict": dict(model.state_dict()), "diagnostics": diagnostics},
               os.environ["SCHOLARLOOP_ARTIFACT"])


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

            super().__init__()

                d, 2, 4 * d, dropout=0.0, batch_first=True, norm_first=True) for _ in range(layers)])
            self.norm, self.out = nn.LayerNorm(d), nn.Linear(d, VOCAB)

        def forward(self, ids):
            n = ids.shape[1]
            h = self.tok(ids) + self.pos(torch.arange(n))
            mask = torch.triu(torch.ones(n, n, dtype=torch.bool), 1)
            for block in self.blocks:

    """Invalid rate (%) of greedy decodes on a frozen split: the share of prompts whose output is
    none of the valid strings. Lower is better."""

    _x_tr, x_val, x_te = _split(fold)
    x = torch.from_numpy(x_te if split == "test" else x_val)
    model.eval()
    y = generate(model, x)[:, LENGTH + 1:]
    valid = (valid_outputs(x) == y).all(-1).any(0)
    return round(float((~valid).float().mean() * 100.0), 4)


def emit_result(value: float, seeds: list[float] | None = None, config: dict | None = None,
                diagnostics: dict | None = None) -> None:
    print("SCHOLARLOOP_RESULT " + json.dumps(
        {"metric_name": METRIC_NAME, "value": float(value),
         "seeds": seeds or [value], "config": config or {}, "diagnostics": diagnostics or {}}))


def score(artifact_path: str, split: str = "val", fold: int = 0) -> None:
    """Trusted metric: rebuild the frozen student from config, load the agent's weights (safely),
    and score greedy decodes on a frozen split."""
    import torch

    bundle = torch.load(artifact_path, weights_only=True)   # state_dict only, no code execution
    cfg = bundle["config"]
    model = build_model(cfg)
    model.load_state_dict(bundle["state_dict"])
    # Numbers train.py chose to report about its own run (e.g. the step a switch fired). They are
    # passed through as self-reported diagnostics and play no part in the metric.
    reported = bundle.get("diagnostics") or {}
    diagnostics = {str(k): float(v) for k, v in reported.items()
                   if isinstance(v, (int, float)) and not isinstance(v, bool) and v == v and abs(v) != float("inf")}
    emit_result(evaluate(model, split, fold), config=cfg, diagnostics=diagnostics)


def parse_score_args(argv: list[str]):
    """`score <artifact> [val|test] [fold]` -> (artifact, split, fold), or None if malformed."""
    if not 2 <= len(argv) <= 4 or argv[0] != "score":
        return None
    split = argv[2] if len(argv) > 2 else "val"
    fold = argv[3] if len(argv) > 3 else "0"
    if split not in ("val", "test") or not fold.isdigit() or int(fold) >= N_FOLDS:
        return None
    return argv[1], split, int(fold)


def _main(argv: list[str]) -> int:
    parsed = parse_score_args(argv)
    if parsed is None:
        print("usage: python -m engines.seq_distill.prepare score <artifact> [test | val [fold]]",
              file=sys.stderr)
        return 2
    score(*parsed)
    return 0

    raise SystemExit(_main(sys.argv[1:]))

from __future__ import annotations

import json
import os

import torch
import torch.nn.functional as F

from engines.seq_distill import prepare

MODE = 'yoked'
HPARAMS = {'lr': 0.003, 'on_policy_frac': 0.0, 'temperature': 1.0}
BATCH = 64
L, A = prepare.LENGTH, prepare.ALPHABET
TARGET_FRAC = 1.0
FIXED_STEP = 1500
TAU_INV = 25.0
PROBE_EVERY = 100
PROBE_N = 256
CAP = 1500
YOKE_OFFSET = 1000


def effective_hparams() -> dict:
    return {**HPARAMS, **json.loads(os.environ.get('SCHOLARLOOP_CONFIG', '{}'))}


def output_logits(model, ids):
    return model(ids[:, :-1])[:, L:, :A]


def token_errors(x, y):
    """Mismatched symbols against the closest valid output (0 means valid), shape [N]."""
    return (prepare.valid_outputs(x) != y.unsqueeze(0)).sum(-1).min(0).values


def probe(student, xp):
    student.eval()
    err = token_errors(xp, prepare.generate(student, xp)[:, L + 1:])
    return float((err > 0).float().mean() * 100.0), float(err.float().mean() / L)


def run(seed, h, mode, switch_at=None, probe_seed=None, stop_at_switch=False):
    torch.manual_seed(seed)
    g = torch.Generator().manual_seed(seed)
    prompts = torch.from_numpy(prepare.load_train())
    teacher = prepare.load_teacher()
    student = prepare.build_model()
    torch.manual_seed(seed)
    for module in student.modules():
        reset = getattr(module, 'reset_parameters', None) or getattr(module, '_reset_parameters', None)
        if reset is not None:
            reset()
    gp = torch.Generator().manual_seed(10000 + (seed if probe_seed is None else probe_seed))
    xp = prompts[torch.randperm(len(prompts), generator=gp)[:PROBE_N]]
    gc = torch.Generator().manual_seed(20000 + seed)
    opt = torch.optim.AdamW(student.parameters(), lr=float(h['lr']))
    tau = float(h['temperature'])
    base_frac = float(h['on_policy_frac'])
    switch_step, forced = -1, 0
    diag = {}
    on_b, err_sum, probes = 0, 0.0, 0
    for step in range(prepare.TRAIN_STEPS):
        if step % PROBE_EVERY == 0:
            inv, tok = probe(student, xp)
            probes += 1
            diag[f'probe_inv_{step:04d}'] = inv
            if switch_step < 0 and mode in ('adaptive', 'corrupt'):
                if inv < TAU_INV:
                    switch_step = step
                elif step >= CAP:
                    switch_step, forced = step, 1
                if switch_step >= 0:
                    diag['probe_inv_at_switch'] = inv
                    diag['probe_tokerr_at_switch'] = tok
                    if stop_at_switch:
                        return switch_step, forced
        if switch_step < 0 and switch_at is not None and step >= switch_at:
            switch_step = step
        frac = TARGET_FRAC if switch_step >= 0 else base_frac
        x = prompts[torch.randint(0, len(prompts), (BATCH,), generator=g)]
        on_policy = torch.rand(1, generator=g).item() < frac
        student.eval()
        if on_policy:
            on_b += 1
            ids = prepare.generate(student, x, sample=True, generator=g)
            p = float(token_errors(x, ids[:, L + 1:]).float().mean() / L)
            err_sum += p
            if mode == 'corrupt':
                pick = torch.randint(0, prepare.N_MODES, (BATCH,), generator=gc)
                y = prepare.valid_outputs(x)[pick, torch.arange(BATCH)]
                flip = torch.rand(y.shape, generator=gc) < p
                shift = torch.randint(1, A, y.shape, generator=gc)
                y = torch.where(flip, (y + shift) % A, y)
                ids = torch.cat([prepare.prompt(x), y], 1)
        else:
            ids = prepare.generate(teacher, x, sample=True, generator=g)
        student.train()
        with torch.no_grad():
            target = F.softmax(output_logits(teacher, ids) / tau, -1)
        log_q = F.log_softmax(output_logits(student, ids) / tau, -1)
        loss = -(target * log_q).sum(-1).mean()
        opt.zero_grad()
        loss.backward()
        opt.step()
    if stop_at_switch:
        return switch_step, forced
    inv, tok = probe(student, xp)
    diag.update({'probe_inv_final': inv, 'probe_tokerr_final': tok, 'switch_step': switch_step,
                 'forced_switch': forced, 'on_policy_batches': on_b,
                 'student_rollout_tokerr_mean': err_sum / max(on_b, 1),
                 'probe_calls': probes + 1, 'train_steps': prepare.TRAIN_STEPS})
    return student, diag


def train_model(seed: int, h: dict):
    if MODE == 'fixed':
        return run(seed, h, 'fixed', switch_at=FIXED_STEP)
    if MODE == 'yoked':
        source_step, source_forced = run(seed, h, 'adaptive', stop_at_switch=True)
        if source_step < 0:
            source_step = prepare.TRAIN_STEPS
        student, diag = run(seed + YOKE_OFFSET, h, 'yoked', switch_at=source_step, probe_seed=seed)
        diag['yoked_source_step'] = source_step
        diag['yoked_source_forced'] = source_forced
        diag['replay_steps'] = min(source_step, prepare.TRAIN_STEPS)
        return student, diag
    return run(seed, h, MODE)


def main() -> None:
    seed = int(os.environ.get('SCHOLARLOOP_SEED', '0'))
    h = effective_hparams()
    model, diagnostics = train_model(seed, h)
    torch.save({'config': h, 'state_dict': dict(model.state_dict()), 'diagnostics': diagnostics},
               os.environ['SCHOLARLOOP_ARTIFACT'])


if __name__ == '__main__':
    main()

"""FROZEN module for the seq-distill engine: task, teacher, student architecture and evaluation.

  1. `load_train()` hands the agent ONLY the training prompts; val and test prompts stay here.
  2. `load_teacher()` returns the frozen teacher. train.py may query it on any token sequence,
     including sequences the student itself generated, but cannot change it.
  3. `build_model()` is frozen and the student's size is fixed here (STUDENT), so no run can
     change capacity: this engine compares training procedures, not model sizes.
  4. `score(artifact)` loads a state_dict with `weights_only=True`, decodes greedily on a frozen
     split and emits the trusted number from pristine ROOT.

Task: a multi-modal string transduction. The input is L=6 symbols from an alphabet of 8. Three
outputs are equally valid: the input copied, the input reversed, and the input reversed with
every symbol incremented (mod 8). The teacher is a 2-layer transformer trained on inputs paired
with one valid output picked uniformly at random, so it models a three-mode distribution. A
student is scored by decoding greedily from the prompt and checking whether the output is one
of the three valid strings; a mixture of modes is invalid. The metric is the invalid rate (%).

A sequence is `x_1..x_L SEP y_1..y_L`. Symbols are token ids 0..7 and SEP is 8. The teacher is
trained once, deterministically, and cached under ~/.cache/scholarloop.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
import os
import sys
from pathlib import Path

import numpy as np

METRIC_NAME = "val_invalid_rate"
N_FOLDS = 5
ALPHABET, LENGTH = 8, 6
SEP, VOCAB = ALPHABET, ALPHABET + 1
SEQ_LEN = 2 * LENGTH + 1
N_MODES = 3
_FOLD_SIZE, _TEST = 500, 2000
_TEACHER = {"d_model": 96, "n_layers": 2}
STUDENT = {"d_model": 32, "n_layers": 2}     # fixed: small enough that training procedures differ
# The step budget every condition is expected to use ($SCHOLARLOOP_DISTILL_STEPS shortens it in tests).
TRAIN_STEPS = int(os.environ.get("SCHOLARLOOP_DISTILL_STEPS", "3000"))
_TEACHER_STEPS, _TEACHER_BATCH, _TEACHER_LR = 8000, 128, 1e-3

def _teacher_path() -> Path:
    root = os.environ.get("SCHOLARLOOP_DATA_DIR") or Path.home() / ".cache" / "scholarloop"
    return Path(root) / "seq-distill-teacher-v1.pt"


def _decode_index(index: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
    """Input number `index` in [0, ALPHABET**LENGTH) as its LENGTH base-ALPHABET digits."""
    return np.stack([(index // ALPHABET ** k) % ALPHABET for k in range(LENGTH)], 1).astype("int64")


def _inputs() -> dict:
    """Every possible input, shuffled once: the first N_FOLDS * _FOLD_SIZE form the pool the folds
    are cut from, the next _TEST are the held-out test, and the teacher trains on the rest."""
    if "inputs" not in _cache:
        order = np.random.RandomState(0).permutation(ALPHABET ** LENGTH)
        pool = N_FOLDS * _FOLD_SIZE
        _cache["inputs"] = {"pool": _decode_index(order[:pool]), "test": _decode_index(order[pool:pool + _TEST]),
                            "teacher": _decode_index(order[pool + _TEST:])}
    return _cache["inputs"]


def _split(fold: int = 0):
    """Training prompts, val prompts (fold `fold` of the pool) and the held-out test prompts."""
    d = _inputs()
    folds = np.arange(len(d["pool"])) // _FOLD_SIZE
    return d["pool"][folds != fold], d["pool"][folds == fold], d["test"]


def _fold_from_env() -> int:
    return int(os.environ.get("SCHOLARLOOP_FOLD", "0"))

            if switch_step < 0 and mode in ('adaptive', 'corrupt'):
                if inv < TAU_INV:
                    switch_step = step
                elif step >= CAP:
                    switch_step, forced = step, 1
                if switch_step >= 0:
                    diag['probe_inv_at_switch'] = inv
                    diag['probe_tokerr_at_switch'] = tok
                    if stop_at_switch:
                        return switch_step, forced
        if switch_step < 0 and switch_at is not None and step >= switch_at:
            switch_step = step
        frac = TARGET_FRAC if switch_step >= 0 else base_frac
        x = prompts[torch.randint(0, len(prompts), (BATCH,), generator=g)]
        on_policy = torch.rand(1, generator=g).item() < frac
        student.eval()
        if on_policy:
            on_b += 1
            ids = prepare.generate(student, x, sample=True, generator=g)
            p = float(token_errors(x, ids[:, L + 1:]).float().mean() / L)
            err_sum += p
            if mode == 'corrupt':
                pick = torch.randint(0, prepare.N_MODES, (BATCH,), generator=gc)
                y = prepare.valid_outputs(x)[pick, torch.arange(BATCH)]
                flip = torch.rand(y.shape, generator=gc) < p
                shift = torch.randint(1, A, y.shape, generator=gc)
                y = torch.where(flip, (y + shift) % A, y)
                ids = torch.cat([prepare.prompt(x), y], 1)
        else:
            ids = prepare.generate(teacher, x, sample=True, generator=g)
        student.train()
        with torch.no_grad():
            target = F.softmax(output_logits(teacher, ids) / tau, -1)
        log_q = F.log_softmax(output_logits(student, ids) / tau, -1)
        loss = -(target * log_q).sum(-1).mean()
        opt.zero_grad()
        loss.backward()
        opt.step()
    if stop_at_switch:
        return switch_step, forced
    inv, tok = probe(student, xp)
    diag.update({'probe_inv_final': inv, 'probe_tokerr_final': tok, 'switch_step': switch_step,
                 'forced_switch': forced, 'on_policy_batches': on_b,
                 'student_rollout_tokerr_mean': err_sum / max(on_b, 1),
                 'probe_calls': probes + 1, 'train_steps': prepare.TRAIN_STEPS})
    return student, diag


def train_model(seed: int, h: dict):
    if MODE == 'fixed':
        return run(seed, h, 'fixed', switch_at=FIXED_STEP)
    if MODE == 'yoked':
        source_step, source_forced = run(seed, h, 'adaptive', stop_at_switch=True)
        if source_step < 0:
            source_step = prepare.TRAIN_STEPS
        student, diag = run(seed + YOKE_OFFSET, h, 'yoked', switch_at=source_step, probe_seed=seed)
        diag['yoked_source_step'] = source_step
        diag['yoked_source_forced'] = source_forced
        diag['replay_steps'] = min(source_step, prepare.TRAIN_STEPS)
        return student, diag
    return run(seed, h, MODE)


def main() -> None:
    seed = int(os.environ.get('SCHOLARLOOP_SEED', '0'))
    h = effective_hparams()
    model, diagnostics = train_model(seed, h)
    torch.save({'config': h, 'state_dict': dict(model.state_dict()), 'diagnostics': diagnostics},
               os.environ['SCHOLARLOOP_ARTIFACT'])


if __name__ == '__main__':
    main()

"""EDITABLE training script for the seq-distill engine.

Builds the (frozen) student via `prepare.build_model`, distills the frozen teacher into it on the
FROZEN training prompts (`prepare.load_train()` never returns val or test), and saves a
`state_dict` + config to $SCHOLARLOOP_ARTIFACT. It does NOT compute or report the metric: the
runner runs the frozen `prepare score` step from pristine ROOT on the artifact. The runner
injects a hyperparameter override via $SCHOLARLOOP_CONFIG.

The default is word-level distillation. Each step draws a batch of prompts, obtains output
sequences for them, and trains the student to match the teacher's next-token distribution at
every output position (forward KL). `on_policy_frac` decides where the output sequences come
from: with that probability a batch is sampled from the STUDENT (on-policy: the teacher labels
the prefixes the student actually produces), otherwise from the TEACHER (off-policy). 0.0 is
pure off-policy, 1.0 pure on-policy.

The student's size is fixed in prepare.py and the step budget is `prepare.TRAIN_STEPS`; keep
both the same in every condition so that conditions differ only in the training procedure.
To record facts about a run (for example the step at which a schedule switched), put numbers
in the `diagnostics` dict returned by `train_model`: they are stored with the result, one value
per seed, as self-reported diagnostics.

Everything about the training procedure is yours to change here: who generates the sequences
and how (sampling temperature, greedy, mixing schedules, replay), the divergence, which
positions or sequences are weighted, the optimizer and schedule. Useful frozen helpers:
`prepare.load_teacher()`, `prepare.generate(model, x, sample=..., temperature=..., generator=...)`,
`prepare.prompt(x)`, `prepare.valid_outputs(x)` (hard labels for the training prompts),
and the constants LENGTH, ALPHABET, SEP. Sequences are `x_1..x_L SEP y_1..y_L`.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
import os

import torch
import torch.nn.functional as F

from engines.seq_distill import prepare

HPARAMS = {
    "lr": 0.003,
    "on_policy_frac": 0.0,
    "temperature": 1.0,
}
BATCH = 64
L, A = prepare.LENGTH, prepare.ALPHABET


def effective_hparams() -> dict:
    return {**HPARAMS, **json.loads(os.environ.get("SCHOLARLOOP_CONFIG", "{}"))}


def output_logits(model, ids):
    """Next-token logits over symbols at the L output positions of full sequences `ids`."""
    return model(ids[:, :-1])[:, L:, :A]


def train_model(seed: int, h: dict):
    torch.manual_seed(seed)
    g = torch.Generator().manual_seed(seed)
    prompts = torch.from_numpy(prepare.load_train())     # training prompts only
    teacher = prepare.load_teacher()                     # frozen
    student = prepare.build_model()                      # frozen architecture and size
    torch.manual_seed(seed)
    for module in student.modules():                     # seed-dependent initialisation
        reset = getattr(module, "reset_parameters", None) or getattr(module, "_reset_parameters", None)
        if reset is not None:
            reset()
    opt = torch.optim.AdamW(student.parameters(), lr=float(h["lr"]))
    tau = float(h["temperature"])
    on_policy_batches = 0
    for _ in range(prepare.TRAIN_STEPS):
        x = prompts[torch.randint(0, len(prompts), (BATCH,), generator=g)]
        on_policy = torch.rand(1, generator=g).item() < float(h["on_policy_frac"])
        on_policy_batches += on_policy
        student.eval()
        ids = prepare.generate(student if on_policy else teacher, x, sample=True, generator=g)
        student.train()
        with torch.no_grad():
            target = F.softmax(output_logits(teacher, ids) / tau, -1)
        log_q = F.log_softmax(output_logits(student, ids) / tau, -1)
        loss = -(target * log_q).sum(-1).mean()          # forward KL up to the teacher's entropy
        opt.zero_grad()
        loss.backward()
        opt.step()
    return student, {"on_policy_batches": on_policy_batches}


def main() -> None:
    seed = int(os.environ.get("SCHOLARLOOP_SEED", "0"))
    h = effective_hparams()
    model, diagnostics = train_model(seed, h)
    torch.save({"config": h, "state_dict": dict(model.state_dict()), "diagnostics": diagnostics},
               os.environ["SCHOLARLOOP_ARTIFACT"])


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

"""FROZEN module for the seq-distill engine: task, teacher, student architecture and evaluation.
Never edit this file. It is the trust anchor:

  1. `load_train()` hands the agent ONLY the training prompts; val and test prompts stay here.
  2. `load_teacher()` returns the frozen teacher. train.py may query it on any token sequence,
     including sequences the student itself generated, but cannot change it.
  3. `build_model()` is frozen and the student's size is fixed here (STUDENT), so no run can
     change capacity: this engine compares training procedures, not model sizes.
  4. `score(artifact)` loads a state_dict with `weights_only=True`, decodes greedily on a frozen
     split and emits the trusted number from pristine ROOT.

Task: a multi-modal string transduction. The input is L=6 symbols from an alphabet of 8. Three
outputs are equally valid: the input copied, the input reversed, and the input reversed with
every symbol incremented (mod 8). The teacher is a 2-layer transformer trained on inputs paired
with one valid output picked uniformly at random, so it models a three-mode distribution. A
student is scored by decoding greedily from the prompt and checking whether the output is one
of the three valid strings; a mixture of modes is invalid. The metric is the invalid rate (%).

A sequence is `x_1..x_L SEP y_1..y_L`. Symbols are token ids 0..7 and SEP is 8. The teacher is
trained once, deterministically, and cached under ~/.cache/scholarloop.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
import os
import sys
from pathlib import Path

import numpy as np

METRIC_NAME = "val_invalid_rate"
N_FOLDS = 5
ALPHABET, LENGTH = 8, 6
SEP, VOCAB = ALPHABET, ALPHABET + 1
SEQ_LEN = 2 * LENGTH + 1
N_MODES = 3
_FOLD_SIZE, _TEST = 500, 2000
_TEACHER = {"d_model": 96, "n_layers": 2}
STUDENT = {"d_model": 32, "n_layers": 2}     # fixed: small enough that training procedures differ
# The step budget every condition is expected to use ($SCHOLARLOOP_DISTILL_STEPS shortens it in tests).
TRAIN_STEPS = int(os.environ.get("SCHOLARLOOP_DISTILL_STEPS", "3000"))
_TEACHER_STEPS, _TEACHER_BATCH, _TEACHER_LR = 8000, 128, 1e-3
_cache: dict = {}


def _teacher_path() -> Path:
    root = os.environ.get("SCHOLARLOOP_DATA_DIR") or Path.home() / ".cache" / "scholarloop"
    return Path(root) / "seq-distill-teacher-v1.pt"


def _decode_index(index: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
    """Input number `index` in [0, ALPHABET**LENGTH) as its LENGTH base-ALPHABET digits."""
    return np.stack([(index // ALPHABET ** k) % ALPHABET for k in range(LENGTH)], 1).astype("int64")


def _inputs() -> dict:
    """Every possible input, shuffled once: the first N_FOLDS * _FOLD_SIZE form the pool the folds
    are cut from, the next _TEST are the held-out test, and the teacher trains on the rest."""
    if "inputs" not in _cache:
        order = np.random.RandomState(0).permutation(ALPHABET ** LENGTH)
        pool = N_FOLDS * _FOLD_SIZE
        _cache["inputs"] = {"pool": _decode_index(order[:pool]), "test": _decode_index(order[pool:pool + _TEST]),
                            "teacher": _decode_index(order[pool + _TEST:])}
    return _cache["inputs"]


def _split(fold: int = 0):
    """Training prompts, val prompts (fold `fold` of the pool) and the held-out test prompts."""
    d = _inputs()
    folds = np.arange(len(d["pool"])) // _FOLD_SIZE
    return d["pool"][folds != fold], d["pool"][folds == fold], d["test"]


def _fold_from_env() -> int:
    return int(os.environ.get("SCHOLARLOOP_FOLD", "0"))


def load_train():
    """Training prompts only: int64 symbols of shape [N, LENGTH]. No outputs are given; ask the
    teacher, or use `valid_outputs` for hard labels."""
    return _split(_fold_from_env())[0]


def valid_outputs(x):
    """The N_MODES valid outputs of each input, shape [N_MODES, N, LENGTH] (torch tensor in and out)."""
    import torch
    return torch.stack([x, x.flip(1), (x.flip(1) + 1) % ALPHABET])


def prompt(x):
    """`x` [N, LENGTH] followed by SEP: the prefix a model continues."""
    import torch
    return torch.cat([x, torch.full((len(x), 1), SEP, dtype=x.dtype)], 1)


def build_model(hparams: dict | None = None):
    """The frozen student: a pre-norm causal transformer of the fixed size STUDENT (2 heads).
    `hparams` is accepted for the engine interface and ignored. `model(ids)` returns next-token
    logits of shape [N, len, VOCAB]."""
    return _transformer(STUDENT)


def _transformer(size: dict):
    import torch
    import torch.nn as nn

    class CausalTransformer(nn.Module):
        def __init__(self, d: int, layers: int):
            super().__init__()
            self.tok, self.pos = nn.Embedding(VOCAB, d), nn.Embedding(SEQ_LEN, d)
            self.blocks = nn.ModuleList([nn.TransformerEncoderLayer(
                d, 2, 4 * d, dropout=0.0, batch_first=True, norm_first=True) for _ in range(layers)])
            self.norm, self.out = nn.LayerNorm(d), nn.Linear(d, VOCAB)

        def forward(self, ids):
            n = ids.shape[1]
            h = self.tok(ids) + self.pos(torch.arange(n))
            mask = torch.triu(torch.ones(n, n, dtype=torch.bool), 1)
            for block in self.blocks:
                h = block(h, src_mask=mask)
            return self.out(self.norm(h))

    torch.manual_seed(0)    # construction is deterministic; train.py reseeds before initialising
    return CausalTransformer(int(size["d_model"]), int(size["n_layers"]))


def generate(model, x, *, sample: bool = False, temperature: float = 1.0, generator=None):
    """Continue each prompt for LENGTH output symbols and return the full sequences [N, SEQ_LEN].
    Greedy by default; with `sample`, draws from the model at `temperature`. No gradients."""
    import torch

    ids = prompt(x)
    with torch.no_grad():
        for _ in range(LENGTH):
            logits = model(ids)[:, -1, :ALPHABET]
            if sample:
                nxt = torch.multinomial(torch.softmax(logits / temperature, -1), 1, generator=generator)
            else:
                nxt = logits.argmax(-1, keepdim=True)
            ids = torch.cat([ids, nxt], 1)
    return ids


def _train_teacher(path: Path) -> None:
    import torch
    import torch.nn.functional as F

    torch.manual_seed(0)
    g = torch.Generator().manual_seed(0)
    inputs = torch.from_numpy(_inputs()["teacher"])          # disjoint from the pool and the test
    model = _transformer(_TEACHER)
    opt = torch.optim.AdamW(model.parameters(), _TEACHER_LR)
    for _ in range(_TEACHER_STEPS):
        x = inputs[torch.randint(0, len(inputs), (_TEACHER_BATCH,), generator=g)]
        mode = torch.randint(0, N_MODES, (_TEACHER_BATCH,), generator=g)
        y = valid_outputs(x)[mode, torch.arange(_TEACHER_BATCH)]
        ids = torch.cat([prompt(x), y], 1)
        logits = model(ids[:, :-1])[:, LENGTH:, :ALPHABET]
        loss = F.cross_entropy(logits.reshape(-1, ALPHABET), y.reshape(-1))
        opt.zero_grad()
        loss.backward()
        opt.step()
    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    tmp = path.with_suffix(".tmp")
    torch.save(dict(model.state_dict()), tmp)
    os.replace(tmp, path)


def load_teacher():
    """The frozen teacher, in eval mode with gradients off. Trained and cached on first use."""
    import torch

    if "teacher" not in _cache:
        path = _teacher_path()
        if not path.exists():
            _train_teacher(path)
        model = _transformer(_TEACHER)
        model.load_state_dict(torch.load(path, weights_only=True))
        model.eval()
        for p in model.parameters():
            p.requires_grad_(False)
        _cache["teacher"] = model
    return _cache["teacher"]


def evaluate(model, split: str = "val", fold: int = 0) -> float:
    """Invalid rate (%) of greedy decodes on a frozen split: the share of prompts whose output is
    none of the valid strings. Lower is better."""
    import torch

    _x_tr, x_val, x_te = _split(fold)
    x = torch.from_numpy(x_te if split == "test" else x_val)
    model.eval()
    y = generate(model, x)[:, LENGTH + 1:]
    valid = (valid_outputs(x) == y).all(-1).any(0)
    return round(float((~valid).float().mean() * 100.0), 4)


def emit_result(value: float, seeds: list[float] | None = None, config: dict | None = None,
                diagnostics: dict | None = None) -> None:
    print("SCHOLARLOOP_RESULT " + json.dumps(
        {"metric_name": METRIC_NAME, "value": float(value),
         "seeds": seeds or [value], "config": config or {}, "diagnostics": diagnostics or {}}))


def score(artifact_path: str, split: str = "val", fold: int = 0) -> None:
    """Trusted metric: rebuild the frozen student from config, load the agent's weights (safely),
    and score greedy decodes on a frozen split."""
    import torch

    bundle = torch.load(artifact_path, weights_only=True)   # state_dict only, no code execution
    cfg = bundle["config"]
    model = build_model(cfg)
    model.load_state_dict(bundle["state_dict"])
    # Numbers train.py chose to report about its own run (e.g. the step a switch fired). They are
    # passed through as self-reported diagnostics and play no part in the metric.
    reported = bundle.get("diagnostics") or {}
    diagnostics = {str(k): float(v) for k, v in reported.items()
                   if isinstance(v, (int, float)) and not isinstance(v, bool) and v == v and abs(v) != float("inf")}
    emit_result(evaluate(model, split, fold), config=cfg, diagnostics=diagnostics)


def parse_score_args(argv: list[str]):
    """`score <artifact> [val|test] [fold]` -> (artifact, split, fold), or None if malformed."""
    if not 2 <= len(argv) <= 4 or argv[0] != "score":
        return None
    split = argv[2] if len(argv) > 2 else "val"
    fold = argv[3] if len(argv) > 3 else "0"
    if split not in ("val", "test") or not fold.isdigit() or int(fold) >= N_FOLDS:
        return None
    return argv[1], split, int(fold)


def _main(argv: list[str]) -> int:
    parsed = parse_score_args(argv)
    if parsed is None:
        print("usage: python -m engines.seq_distill.prepare score <artifact> [test | val [fold]]",
              file=sys.stderr)
        return 2
    score(*parsed)
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(_main(sys.argv[1:]))

argument.question: On the multimodal-transduction-L6-A8 seq-distill task, does switching from off-policy to on-policy training when the student's own probe invalid rate falls below a threshold lower val_invalid_rate compared with pure off-policy, pure on-policy and a fixed-step switch? If it does, does the benefit depend on the trigger responding to the student's state, and on the student's own prefixes?
argument.method_summary: One pre-registered falsification protocol was run with six arms, each at full fidelity over five seed–fold pairs. Seed i was trained on the training prompts of cross-validation fold i and evaluated on that fold's val prompts, so seed and fold are confounded and no arm was evaluated on a single fold. Learning rate, temperature, forward-KL loss and step budget were the same in every arm, and the student architecture and teacher were frozen. The arms were: off_policy_ref (reference); pure_on_policy; a fixed switch to fully on-policy at a mid-run step; an adaptive arm that switches to fully on-policy once the greedy invalid rate on a training-prompt probe batch drops below threshold, with a forced-switch cap; a yoked replay that switches at the adaptive arm's firing step but trains on a different seed; and a corrupted-prefix arm that uses the same trigger but replaces post-switch prefixes with ground truth under token substitution. The trusted metric is val_invalid_rate from the frozen scorer. The analysis reports descriptive paired mean differences against off_policy_ref, with no inferential test. Probe trajectories, switch steps and on-policy batch counts are self-reported by train.py and are not verified by the scorer. The author decided to run no further experiments. This revision therefore narrows the argument: two control comparisons and one mechanism hypothesis are withdrawn as claims and moved to the limitations.

claims.text:
Mean validation invalid rate (%) over five seeds, with seed SD, was:
- off_policy_ref: 14.0 (3.234192)
- pure_on_policy: 9.04 (8.478679)
- fixed_switch_1500: 15.0 (3.896152)
- adaptive_tau25: 12.88 (2.229798)
- yoked_replay: 11.0 (8.866792)
- corrupt_prefix: 12.76 (6.582401)
claims.scope: multimodal-transduction-L6-A8, fixed small student, five seeds per arm, validation folds

claims.text: The adaptive-switch arm had a lower mean val_invalid_rate (12.88) than off_policy_ref (14.0), a paired mean difference of -1.12. The per-seed paired differences were small and mixed in sign: four of the five seed–fold pairs were within about one point of zero, and one of those four was positive. Most of the mean improvement comes from the single pair where off_policy_ref had its highest value (18.4). The improvement is small relative to the seed–fold spread and is not robust across pairs.
claims.scope: One task and one student size. Five seed–fold pairs (seed i trained and evaluated on fold i), so seed and fold variation are confounded. A single adaptive setting. Descriptive only.

claims.text: The adaptive-switch arm did not beat pure_on_policy on mean val_invalid_rate: pure_on_policy averaged 9.04 and the adaptive arm averaged 12.88. The pre-registered prediction that the adaptive switch would be below both pure regimes by a margin therefore fails for the on-policy endpoint. The adaptive arm had the narrower spread across seed–fold pairs.
claims.scope: The same five seed–fold pairs in both arms. The recorded analysis does not pair these two arms directly; each is paired only against off_policy_ref.

claims.text: pure_on_policy had a paired mean difference of -4.96 against off_policy_ref, but the per-pair pattern was heterogeneous. On three of five seed–fold pairs it was much better than off-policy, reaching values of 4.6, 2.6 and 4.2. On one pair it was about equal. On the remaining pair it was clearly worse (23.2 against the reference's 15.8). The direction is not uniform and the spread is large, so the sign of the mean difference is not established at this sample size.
claims.scope: Five seed–fold pairs on one task. No interval was computed for the paired mean difference.

claims.text: The fixed-step switch arm had the highest mean val_invalid_rate of all arms (15.0), a paired mean difference of 1.0 against off_policy_ref. The paired differences were mixed in sign: three of the five seed–fold pairs were worse than the reference and two were better, and the mean difference is within the seed–fold spread. The direction of the fixed-step arm relative to pure off-policy is therefore not established. The adaptive arm (12.88) had a lower mean than the fixed-step arm, which formally satisfies the prediction that adaptive is no worse than the fixed switch. This contrast confounds trigger responsiveness with switch timing: according to self-reported diagnostics, the adaptive switches fired earlier than the fixed step on every seed, so the adaptive arm spent more of training on-policy.
claims.scope: Only one fixed step was tested, and the switch-step curve is unmapped. Five seed–fold pairs.

claims.text: According to self-reported diagnostics, the adaptive trigger fired before the forced-switch cap on all five seed–fold pairs, and no switch was forced. On-policy batches occurred only after the reported switch step. The adaptive mechanism was therefore exercised in this run, rather than every switch coming from the cap.
claims.scope: Self-reported diagnostics from train.py (forced_switch, switch_step, on_policy_batches), not verified by the scorer.

claims.text: The pre-registered falsifying outcome was met. The adaptive-switch arm did not beat the better pure regime: pure_on_policy had the lower mean (9.04 against 12.88), so the adaptive switch was not better than the better pure regime by more than the seed–fold spread. The prediction that the adaptive arm would beat both pure regimes is therefore not supported in this configuration. The two controls meant to test why a trigger might help (yoked replay and corrupted prefixes) did not implement their intended contrasts and support no conclusion either way (see limitations). The conservative reading is that this experiment does not distinguish the switching rules.
claims.scope: Limited to this task, student size, single adaptive setting and five seed–fold pairs. This is a negative result for the tested configuration, not evidence against adaptive switching in general.

limitations: Evaluation scope (corrected from the previous version): seed i was trained and evaluated on cross-validation fold i, so training prompts, probe prompts and the val set all change with the seed. The spread across seeds is seed-plus-fold variation. Nothing was evaluated on a single fold. Paired differences against the reference pair on both seed and fold.

Withdrawn claim (claim_corrupt_recovers_gain): the corrupted-prefix control set its substitution rate from its own student's sampled rollout error, not the adaptive student's. Because that student drifted to higher rollout error than the adaptive student on every seed (self-reported student_rollout_tokerr_mean), the control did not implement the specified matched noise level. Its post-switch prefixes were also exact ground truth rather than teacher samples. Its mean paired gain is also dominated by the same outlying reference pair as the adaptive gain. It is no longer treated as a test of whether the benefit needs the student's own prefixes; that question is unanswered.

Withdrawn claim (claim_yoked_matches_or_beats): the yoked replay arm trained on different seeds from the reference and adaptive arms. Its recorded per-seed differences are therefore not paired observations, and only a difference of means can be reported. That difference does not separate yoked from adaptive given the yoked arm's large spread, and the yoked students switched in different training states from their adaptive sources. Whether online responsiveness adds value beyond switch timing is untested.

Withdrawn claim (claim_variance_mechanism_hypothesis): the previous version proposed that more training on student-generated or noisy prefixes yields more seed-dependent outcomes. The data contradict this premise. The adaptive and yoked arms had identical on-policy batch counts yet very different spreads, and with five values per arm the spread estimates cannot rank variance. No mode-commitment diagnostic was recorded, and no mechanism for the dispersion is claimed.

Correction to claim_pure_on_high_variance: the earlier wording said the mean advantage rested on a 'minority' of seeds. In fact three of five pairs were much better, one about equal and one worse. The point that the sign of the mean difference is not established is kept.

Only five seed–fold pairs per arm, with no inferential test and no interval on any paired difference. Each value comes from a single evaluation on a few hundred val prompts, and the binomial evaluation noise is of the same order as the adaptive-versus-reference mean difference. 'Within noise' was never quantified.

Only one adaptive setting (one probe threshold, full on-policy target) and one fixed switch step were run. The threshold sweep, partial targets, the static mixed-fraction arm and the other fixed steps were omitted.

setup.text: Task multimodal-transduction-L6-A8: each input is L=6 symbols from an alphabet of 8. Three outputs are valid: the copy, the reversal, and the reversal incremented mod 8. A mixture of modes counts as invalid.
The metric val_invalid_rate is the percentage of greedy student decodes on a validation fold that match none of the valid outputs. Lower is better. Each validation fold holds 500 prompts.

The student is a frozen-architecture pre-norm causal transformer with d_model 32, 2 layers and 2 heads. The frozen teacher has d_model 96 and 2 layers, trained for 8000 steps on inputs disjoint from the fold pool and the test set.
Every arm trains for 3000 steps with batch 64 using AdamW at lr 0.003. The loss is forward KL between teacher and student next-token distributions at temperature 1.0 over output positions.
Each arm ran five seeds (zero through four) over five cross-validation folds at full fidelity. Run records list fold indices alongside seed indices, so seed and fold vary together.
Each full-fidelity run had a time budget of 1200 seconds.
The off_policy_ref arm runs the unmodified script with on_policy_frac 0, so the teacher samples every training prefix.
The pure_on_policy arm sets on_policy_frac to 1 throughout, so the student samples every prefix and the teacher labels it.
The fixed_switch_1500 arm uses on_policy_frac 0 before step 1500 and 1.0 afterwards. A probe runs every 100 steps for logging only.

In the adaptive_tau25 arm, a probe greedily decodes 256 training prompts every 100 steps. When the probe invalid rate falls below 25%, on_policy_frac switches from 0 to 1.0. The switch is forced at step 1500 if the trigger has not fired.

The yoked_replay arm first replays the adaptive run for the seed to find its firing step. It then trains a fresh student from training seed seed+1000 and switches to on_policy_frac 1.0 at exactly that step, ignoring the probe.

The corrupt_prefix arm uses the adaptive trigger and cap. After the switch, it samples student rollouts to measure per-token error p, then trains on ground-truth outputs (mode chosen uniformly) with each symbol substituted at rate p.

Registered prediction: adaptive_tau25 is at least 1.0 point below both pure regimes and below the 8.8 hard-label baseline, and no worse than fixed_switch_1500. yoked_replay is within noise of adaptive or worse. corrupt_prefix recovers less than half of the adaptive gain over off_policy_ref.
Analysis: for each arm, per-seed paired mean differences against off_policy_ref, read descriptively beside the seed spread, with no inferential test.
The profile declares a val_invalid_rate of 8.8 for a hard-label training baseline. That baseline was not re-run in this protocol.

Registered falsification: the hypothesis fails if adaptive_tau25 does not beat the better of off_policy_ref and pure_on_policy by more than the seed standard deviation, or if both yoked_replay and corrupt_prefix match it. A trigger that fires only through the cap on every seed leaves responsiveness untested.

Every possible input is shuffled once. Five folds of 500 prompts each are cut from the start of that order, the next 2000 prompts form the held-out test set, and the teacher trains on the rest. A run on one fold validates on that fold and trains on the prompts of the other four.

Training prefixes are sampled, not decoded greedily: each batch draws its output sequences from either the teacher or the student at sampling temperature 1.0, and on_policy_frac is the probability that a batch uses the student.
Each arm's run record lists 5 training attempts for its five seeds.

The teacher is trained once with a fixed seed for 8000 steps of AdamW at lr 1e-3 and batch 128. Each training target is one valid output chosen uniformly at random from the three modes, and the loss is cross-entropy over output positions.
The frozen protocol records the software environment: Python 3.12.9, torch 2.11.0 and numpy 2.2.6.
The probe batch is a fixed subset of 256 training prompts, drawn once per run from a generator seeded with 10000 plus the run seed. The probe and the evaluation decode greedily.

Per-token error p is the smallest number of positions at which a sampled student rollout differs from any valid output, divided by the output length. It is computed on each post-switch batch. Corruption draws use a generator seeded with 20000 plus the run seed.

related_work.text: GKD trains students on a mixture of fixed and self-generated sequences with a static student-data fraction. This study keeps that fraction knob but switches it once during training, conditioned on the student's probe invalid rate.

Imitation-learning distillation treats the teacher as an oracle on student-visited states to address exposure bias. This study designed a corrupted-prefix control to test that account. The control's corruption rate tracked its own student's rollout error, not the adaptive student's, so it yields no conclusion and the account remains untested here.
Sequence-level KD trains on teacher-generated outputs and is the canonical off-policy baseline. This study's reference arm is off-policy word-level distillation on teacher-sampled prefixes.
MiniLLM changes both the divergence (reverse KL) and the sampling distribution. This study holds the forward-KL loss fixed and varies only the prefix source and its schedule.

DASH-OPD and DTDD switch adaptively between teacher and student within rollouts, using discrepancy signals. This study instead makes a single, one-way, training-schedule switch gated by a probe invalid rate. Their abstracts do not describe yoked or corrupted-prefix controls.
A controlled study on GSM8K argues that the state distribution supervised matters alongside the loss. This study varies only the state source, on a non-language transduction task.
Mask Forcing perturbs student self-rollouts in video diffusion distillation. This study's corrupted-prefix arm perturbs ground-truth discrete prefixes as a control, not as a method.
Instance-level curriculum distillation orders training instances using an earlier student snapshot. This study schedules the policy that generates prefixes rather than the order of instances.

Prior work reports that student-generated outputs are costly and hard to optimise when the student is much smaller than the teacher. This study uses one fixed small student and does not vary the capacity gap.

Entropy-aware on-policy distillation reports instability of reverse-KL signals under high teacher entropy. This study's teacher models a three-mode distribution, but teacher entropy was not measured or varied.

reports.summary: Implementation-lens review, round 10. All setup statements match the versioned code and run records. Every claim's numbers and per-seed descriptions match the measurements. The withdrawn controls are handled as limitations, and the self-reported, non-scorer-verified status of the diagnostics is disclosed. issues.observation: yoked_replay trains on seed+1000. The contrast therefore mixes responsiveness with seed and fold variance, as well as with the arbitrary state at the yoked step. The negative conclusion ('no support for responsiveness') is fine, but the contrast has almost no discriminating power at this n.
issues.required_action: Stop presenting the yoked deltas as paired. Report yoked versus adaptive as an unpaired comparison with an interval. issues.observation: Every run record lists folds [0,1,2,3,4] next to seed_ids [0,1,2,3,4], and the analysis caveat says seed and fold observations may be dependent. 'Seed variance' would then be partly fold variance, and the scope statements are wrong. Separately, each value comes from a single evaluation on 500 prompts, which carries about 1.5 pt binomial SE at about 13% invalid. That is comparable to the -1.12 adaptive effect, and no 'within noise' threshold was ever quantified.

feedback: Author decision, unchanged: no further experiments; resolve issues by narrowing. This revision only adds reproducibility statements, as the falsification reviewer required: setup_teacher_training (teacher targets, loss, optimiser, learning rate, batch size, steps, fixed seed), setup_environment (recorded Python, torch and numpy versions), setup_probe (probe subset, its seeding, greedy decoding) and setup_token_error (definition of per-token error and corruption seeding), plus one limitation saying that implementation details not restated are fixed in the frozen scorer and versioned scripts. Claims and earlier limitations stand word for word; the author keeps the approved claim wording and accepts the minor notes about claim length and scope as notes.

mandatory_limitations: Evaluation scope (corrected from the previous version): seed i was trained and evaluated on cross-validation fold i, so training prompts, probe prompts and the val set all change with the seed. The spread across seeds is seed-plus-fold variation. Nothing was evaluated on a single fold. Paired differences against the reference pair on both seed and fold.

Withdrawn claim (claim_corrupt_recovers_gain): the corrupted-prefix control set its substitution rate from its own student's sampled rollout error, not the adaptive student's. Because that student drifted to higher rollout error than the adaptive student on every seed (self-reported student_rollout_tokerr_mean), the control did not implement the specified matched noise level. Its post-switch prefixes were also exact ground truth rather than teacher samples. Its mean paired gain is also dominated by the same outlying reference pair as the adaptive gain. It is no longer treated as a test of whether the benefit needs the student's own prefixes; that question is unanswered.

Withdrawn claim (claim_yoked_matches_or_beats): the yoked replay arm trained on different seeds from the reference and adaptive arms. Its recorded per-seed differences are therefore not paired observations, and only a difference of means can be reported. That difference does not separate yoked from adaptive given the yoked arm's large spread, and the yoked students switched in different training states from their adaptive sources. Whether online responsiveness adds value beyond switch timing is untested.

Withdrawn claim (claim_variance_mechanism_hypothesis): the previous version proposed that more training on student-generated or noisy prefixes yields more seed-dependent outcomes. The data contradict this premise. The adaptive and yoked arms had identical on-policy batch counts yet very different spreads, and with five values per arm the spread estimates cannot rank variance. No mode-commitment diagnostic was recorded, and no mechanism for the dispersion is claimed.

Correction to claim_pure_on_high_variance: the earlier wording said the mean advantage rested on a 'minority' of seeds. In fact three of five pairs were much better, one about equal and one worse. The point that the sign of the mean difference is not established is kept.

Only five seed–fold pairs per arm, with no inferential test and no interval on any paired difference. Each value comes from a single evaluation on a few hundred val prompts, and the binomial evaluation noise is of the same order as the adaptive-versus-reference mean difference. 'Within noise' was never quantified.

Only one adaptive setting (one probe threshold, full on-policy target) and one fixed switch step were run. The threshold sweep, partial targets, the static mixed-fraction arm and the other fixed steps were omitted.
The adaptive versus fixed-switch contrast is confounded with total on-policy duration.
The yoked and corrupt arms do not match the other arms in compute: the yoked arm spends replay compute and the corrupt arm discards student rollouts. No compute-matched total was recorded.
Probe trajectories, switch steps, on-policy batch counts and per-token error rates are self-reported by train.py and not verified by the scorer. The probe uses training prompts, not val.
Single synthetic task, single tiny fixed student, single divergence. The results do not generalise beyond this setting.
No arm's mean reached the profile's declared hard-label baseline. That baseline was not re-measured in this study, so the comparison is indicative only.
